cases.requirement: Tested upstream index.ts sha256 equals the pin and an adjacent package.json, if present, says 0.4.2.
A real Pi 1.3.0 SDK session loads upstream through an inline factory, memory tools are active, a scripted fixture turn executes a real tool, and no built-in tool is active.
Stat sentinels on real ~/.pi and qmd stores are unchanged, and the qmd index exists only inside the isolated run directory.
Automatic resource discovery stays off: trap extensions in cwd/.pi/extensions and agentDir/extensions never execute.
session.dispose() fires upstream session_shutdown, so host-managed per-run sessions get lifecycle cleanup.
Shared dir: memory_read from A does not expose B's value for the same logical slot, and vice versa.
Shared dir: the prompt injected into a fresh A session excludes B's value.
Shared dir: memory_search from A excludes B's value after a real qmd update.
Shared dir: forgetting the slot from A preserves B's value.
Shared dir: correcting A with overwrite preserves B's value.
Per-project store: each project's memory_read shows only its own value.
Per-project store: each project's injected prompt contains its own value and not the other's.
Per-project store: search returns its own value and never the other's, using isolated qmd indexes.
Per-project store: forgetting the slot in A removes A's value and preserves B's.
Per-project store: correcting A leaves B unchanged.
Unknown, empty and traversal project IDs fail closed before any store or process is created.
Global memory never reaches a project prompt implicitly and is reachable only through the explicit global scope.
A recovery ID from A cannot restore through B.
Same process, two stores through the upstream _setBaseDir seam: a write by session A lands in A's store when B was opened after A.
Same process, two stores: session A's injected snapshot does not contain B's value after B opens.
Concurrent A and B work in separate processes produces no cross-store write or prompt leak.
A Chinese correction written with default mode replaces the old value. The semantics are recorded either way.
overwrite correction removes the old value without destroying unrelated entries or skipping recovery.
Forgetting the default target and writing the new value excludes the old value recorded in today's daily log from a fresh prompt.
Explicit forget of long_term and today's daily plus a new write gives a fresh prompt and read with the new value only.
After COR-04 and a real qmd update, the Chinese query retrieves the new record and excludes the stale one.
Forgetting today's log also stops yesterday's old value reaching a fresh prompt.
After correction in the same session, the next model request no longer carries the old value in prior session context.
In default stable mode, a corrected value written mid-session reaches this session's injected prompt on the next turn.
Writing the same record twice is idempotent.
A late stale write of the old value after correction is rejected or superseded.
Forgetting by a Chinese paraphrase of the old wording removes the old value.
An overbroad forget match does not remove the new corrected value.
Adapter correct(): the old value is gone from long_term, today and yesterday, and the new value is in a fresh prompt.
Adapter write with a repeated operationId applies once.
Adapter rejects a late write carrying a superseded epoch, including after a process restart.
After adapter correct() in the same session, the next model request no longer carries the old value from prior session context.
Immediately after forget: source file clean, memory_read clean, this session's next injected prompt clean, and a fresh session's prompt clean.
The forget tool result does not put the forgotten value into the next model request.
With adapter redaction, the forget tool result does not put the forgotten value into the next model request.
Before qmd refresh, memory_search does not return the forgotten value.
In per-turn mode before qmd refresh, the injected prompt does not contain the forgotten value.
After a real qmd update, memory_search does not return the forgotten value and an unrelated entry stays retrievable.
A fresh OS process reopening persisted data shows no forgotten value in file, read or prompt, and nothing is restored automatically.
A fresh OS process reopening the persisted index does not return the forgotten value from memory_search.
Recovery JSON is excluded from normal search after a real qmd update.
Forget physically erases the value from the store. Retained recovery payload is disclosed as a GAP.
With exit summary disabled, the shutdown handler makes no model request and does not bring the value back.
With exit summary enabled and a labelled fixture summary, the shutdown handler neither sends the forgotten value to a model nor persists it.
The compaction handler after full forget does not bring the value back.
The compaction handler after default-target forget does not re-copy the value still in the daily log.
memory_forget can remove the same fact recorded in the scratchpad, or it stays out of the prompt.
pi-memory provides a read-only mode under which memory_forget and memory_write do not mutate files.
A host tool allowlist without mutating memory tools prevents a scripted memory_forget call from mutating files.
The adapter read-only tool_call block prevents a scripted memory_forget call from mutating files.
Malformed, traversal and well-formed-but-missing recovery IDs return errors and change nothing.
An explicit restore is idempotent: a second call does not duplicate entries.
Positive control: a Chinese exact-run query returns the matching record.
A Chinese substring of the run returns the matching record.
Positive control: an ASCII tag query returns the matching record.
Negative control: unrelated Chinese and absent-token queries return nothing.
Near-topic negative control: a query sharing topic words returns nothing.
A query beginning with -- is treated as text, not as a qmd flag: no alternate index is created.
Without qmd: memory_search returns an error, core tools still work and the prompt still assembles.
First run on a missing memory directory registers the qmd collection at session start.
